questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which bee contains only 16 chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Drone bee is haploid. It has only 16 chromosomes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: From where is royal jelly produced?
options: from the gland at the head of queen bee
from the gland at the head of drone bee
from the gland at the head of worker bee
from the salivary gland of worker
questions.explanation: Royal jelly is produced by worker bees. It comes from glands in their head.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which bee is formed when the larva is fed royal jelly continuously?
questions.explanation: A larva fed royal jelly continuously becomes queen. Food decides the queen development.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which stage of the bee is shown in the given diagram in the textbook?
questions.explanation: Pupa is the resting stage. In this stage, the bee changes into adult form.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is honey bee called a social insect?
options: It helps in pollination in plants
questions.explanation: Honey bee lives and works in a colony. So it is called a social insect.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When the pollen baskets in the legs of worker bees are broken, which function cannot be performed by them?
questions.explanation: Pollen baskets help worker bees collect pollen. If they break, pollen collection cannot happen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is the characteristic of the drone bee?
questions.explanation: Drone bee is haploid and fertile. It is male and helps in mating.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where does the queen bee store the sperms received from the drone bee after the nuptial flight?
questions.explanation: Queen stores sperm in the sperm sac. She uses it later to fertilize eggs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: To which phylum does a honey bee belong?
questions.explanation: Honey bee has jointed legs. So it belongs to phylum Arthropoda.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is apiculture according to the chapter context?
questions.explanation: Apiculture means keeping and farming bees. It is done for honey, wax and pollination.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which three types of bees live in a hive?
questions.explanation: A hive has queen, drone and worker bees. Each type has a different work.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is the body of a honey bee divided?
questions.explanation: Honey bee body has three parts. They are head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What type of eyes do honey bees have on the head?
questions.explanation: Honey bees have compound eyes. These eyes help them see many directions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many pairs of legs arise from the thorax of a honey bee?
questions.explanation: Honey bee has three pairs of legs. All legs come from the thorax.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which structure is present on the legs of worker bees for collecting pollen?
questions.explanation: Worker bees have pollen baskets on legs. These baskets help collect pollen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which type of bee is the largest and elongated in the beehive?
questions.explanation: Queen bee is the largest and longest bee. Her main work is laying eggs.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement describes the head and abdomen of the queen bee?
options: Head is larger and square, abdomen has pollen baskets
Head is smaller and rounded, abdomen is smooth and covered with hairs
Abdomen is divided into roots and leaves
questions.explanation: Queen has a small rounded head and smooth abdomen. These features help identify her.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main function of the queen bee in the hive?
options: Control all bees and lay eggs
questions.explanation: Queen controls the hive and lays eggs. She is the main female bee.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which special scented substance is produced by the queen bee to control hive activities?
questions.explanation: Pheromone is a scented chemical. Queen uses it to control hive activities.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How do worker bees form a new queen?
options: By reducing the egg stage to one day
By feeding royal jelly to the larva
questions.explanation: Worker bees feed royal jelly to larva. This special food can form a new queen.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is a drone bee described in comparison to the queen and worker?
options: Smaller than queen but larger than worker
questions.explanation: Drone is smaller than queen but larger than worker. It is the male bee.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which structure is absent in the drone bee according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Drone bee has no sting. So it cannot sting like worker bee.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which function does the drone bee perform?
questions.explanation: Drone's main work is mating with queen. It fertilizes the queen bee.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: From what type of egg is the drone developed?
questions.explanation: Drone develops from an unfertilized egg. That is why it is haploid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the development of drone from unfertilized egg called?
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis means development from unfertilized egg. Drone bees form by this process.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which bee is the smallest in the hive?
questions.explanation: Worker bee is the smallest bee in the hive. It does most of the work.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What type of mouthparts do worker bees have?
questions.explanation: Worker bees have chewing and lapping mouthparts. They use them for wax work and nectar feeding.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are worker bees called hardworking in the chapter?
options: They do not work outside the hive
They collect nectar, construct hive, nurse young and protect hive
questions.explanation: Worker bees do many jobs. They collect nectar, build hive, nurse young and guard the hive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: About how many worker bees can be found in a hive?
questions.explanation: A hive may have 20,000-30,000 workers. Workers are the largest group in the hive.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the approximate life span of worker bees according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Worker bees live for about 6 weeks to 6 months. Their life depends on work and season.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which are the four stages of the honey bee life cycle?
questions.explanation: Honey bee life cycle has four stages. They are egg, larva, pupa and adult.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the transformation from egg to larva, pupa and adult called in honey bees?
questions.explanation: Complete metamorphosis has egg, larva, pupa and adult stages. Honey bee shows all these stages.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which two events occur during the life cycle due to metamorphosis?
questions.explanation: Histolysis breaks old larval tissues. Histogenesis forms new adult tissues.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When does the queen usually leave for the mating flight?
questions.explanation: Queen usually goes for mating flight in the evening. This flight is called nuptial flight.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to drones after mating with the queen?
options: They die because their genital organs are pulled during mating
questions.explanation: Drone dies after mating. Its reproductive organ is pulled out during mating.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where are sperms stored in the body of the queen bee?
questions.explanation: Queen stores sperm in spermathecae. This storage helps her fertilize eggs later.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many eggs can a queen lay per day under favourable conditions?
questions.explanation: Queen can lay up to 3,000 eggs per day. This happens in favourable conditions.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What develops from fertilized eggs in honey bees?
questions.explanation: Fertilized eggs form queen and worker bees. Both are female bees.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What develops from unfertilized eggs in honey bees?
questions.explanation: Unfertilized eggs form drone bees. Drones are male bees.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How long does the egg stage last in all bees?
questions.explanation: Egg stage lasts three days. This is the same for all bees.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which bee has the shortest total development period from egg to adult?
options: All take exactly the same time
questions.explanation: Queen develops the fastest. It takes the shortest time to become adult.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many days does the queen bee take to become adult from egg?
questions.explanation: Queen becomes adult in 16 days. This is shorter than worker and drone.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many days does the worker bee take to become adult from egg?
questions.explanation: Worker bee becomes adult in 21 days. This is longer than queen but shorter than drone.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How many days does the drone take to become adult from egg?
questions.explanation: Drone becomes adult in 24 days. It takes the longest development time.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: During which stage does a bee not feed or move but undergo structural changes?
questions.explanation: Pupa does not feed or move. Inside, its body changes into adult form.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What work do newly born worker bees do for about 1-3 days?
options: Clean the hive and provide warmth to eggs and larva
questions.explanation: New workers clean the hive and warm eggs and larvae. This is their first work.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What do worker bees mainly do at 4-6 days of age?
questions.explanation: At 4-6 days, workers feed larvae. They give honey bread to larvae.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What develops in worker bees around 12-17 days?
questions.explanation: Wax glands develop around 12-17 days. These glands help workers make wax.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: After about 21 days, what do worker bees generally collect?
questions.explanation: After about 21 days, workers go outside. They collect nectar, pollen and water.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best shows the importance of honey bees to humans and ecosystems?
options: They help in pollination, produce honey and beeswax, and support income
They are useful only for producing smoke
questions.explanation: Honey bees help in pollination and give honey and wax. They also support income.
